title: Anthropic launches Claude for Manufacturers ahead of IPO
excerpt: Anthropic launched a new Claude for Manufacturers plugin, part of its attempt to boost adoption of Claude as its huge IPO looms.
content_html:
Anthropic pitches a new Claude tool as a salve for manufacturers' labor shortages

By Stephen Council

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

Anthropic has a new target for Claude adoption: people who run the factory floor.

The company launched a new Claude for Manufacturers plugin on Thursday. It's a cluster of add-ons that make the company's AI tool better for quality engineers, technicians, and other workers who run production lines. Although it won't directly operate equipment — that's another initiative the company is researching — it represents another industry-specific foray by the AI company.

In the lead-up to its trillion-dollar initial public offering, expected next week, Anthropic has a playbook. To boost revenue and adoption of its AI models, the company is releasing tools and connectors tailored to different workers: there are Claude models for healthcare, financial services, legal, government, and more. The manufacturing release fits the same strategy.

"Manufacturing is complex and judgment-heavy work," Lauren Collett, Anthropic's enterprise go-to-market leader, told Business Insider. "And I think that as model capabilities have advanced, this is just a really, really great time for us to be looking at some of these more complex business processes."

She said Anthropic heard from manufacturing customers that they have "more work than their experienced people have time to get through," so part of the hope is that the plugins will speed up repetitive tasks.

Anthropic's launch includes 17 skills, which are ready-made Claude setups designed to complete specific tasks. The plugin for manufacturers also connects Claude to the design software Autodesk Fusion and to Infor, which can help businesses with procurement.

Anthropic is pitching to people who run factories

The manufacturing plugin's skills include quoting a new job, diagnosing a machine's breakdown, sourcing equipment from a supplier, and compiling production data. A skill gives Claude instructions, making it more likely that the AI system will finish what a person wants.

Collett said she hopes that the tools can reduce the "back-office toil" that slows businesses down.

For example, if a part fails inspection, Claude could automatically document what happened, check past reports or email histories for the same defect, rank the likely causes, draft the correction report, and then hand that to the job's quality engineer, Collett said.

She also said that over time, Anthropic would likely add more connectors to other software that manufacturers use, beyond the set in this launch.

Anthropic, after its smash hit with Claude Code, has been pushing the use of its tools for other knowledge work. Its pitch to investors for its IPO relies on the idea that many industries could adopt the company's AI tools.

"Experienced people are hard to find," Collett said, "and so there's a really big opportunity for them to get better leverage out of the folks that they have today, giving them more time for the decisions that need their judgment."
